scope: Canonical artwork-bearing homepage, docs, watch, and 404 routes
All 12 static HTML routes in the local route surface
390 and 1440 viewport widths in light and dark themes
Lazy/reveal loading, keyboard focus, mobile menu, theme toggle, normal/reduced motion
Rendered screenshots, selected image loads, horizontal overflow, and console/request errors
Synthetic intercepted signup success/error, malformed JSON, and string-ok responses

expected_picture_candidate_abort.detail: One non-selected desktop map picture candidate reported net::ERR_ABORTED; selected currentSrc loaded and document width remained bounded.

automated_matrix.overflow_normalization: Descendants of .table-scroll and .code-block are intentionally wider than a narrow viewport for keyboard/touch horizontal scrolling; document scrollWidth remained equal to the viewport.

signup_mocks.success_case: 390 light: one intercepted same-origin POST returned JSON ok=true; form reset, status became success, subscribe-confirm.png loaded at 400x300, and document width stayed bounded.
signup_mocks.error_case: 1440 dark: one intercepted same-origin POST returned ok=false; generic error state remained, no confirmation artwork was appended, and document width stayed bounded.

checks: JSON ok='true' string stayed in error state, did not append art, and did not reset the form.
Malformed JSON stayed in generic error state, did not append art, and did not reset the form.

observations: Homepage hero is edge-to-edge at desktop and uses the portrait crop at 390; report poster and Watch/Build diagrams stay legible and stack without clipping.
Docs capabilities illustration and conceptual route map remain legible in both themes; the narrow capability table is contained in its horizontal scroll region.
Watch presents the unavailable artwork and report-only status without a player or live indicator; 404.html presents its artwork, clear status, branded header, and footer.
Dark theme surfaces, text, status labels, borders, focus rings, controls, and artwork placements remained readable in inspected renders.
The synthetic signup success artwork fits the mobile form and leaves the viewport width bounded.

findings.title: Legacy shells omit the branded header and theme controls
findings.details: home.html contains the favicon but no mark or site header and immediately meta-refreshes to index.html. The directly served 404.shtml contains the 404 artwork and favicon but no mark, header, menu, theme control, or footer; its dark-context render remains light. Canonical /404.html is fully branded and passed the matrix.
findings.recommendation: Add the shared compact header/mark and dark/theme treatment to the legacy and server fallback shells, or remove those shells from the served route contract, then rerun the header scan and direct fallback screenshots.

limitations: This is a loopback static preview; it does not establish deployment, hosting injection behavior, public availability, or publication authority.
External origins were blocked. No PHP/API request was allowed through and no real email or production form submission occurred.
Automated axe and rendered screenshots supplement assistive-technology review and 200% zoom review; neither was claimed here.
The receipt covers the canonical artwork routes and records legacy shell exceptions explicitly; it is not a release approval while W03-F01 remains open.
disposition: Canonical artwork integration is visually and interactively verified locally at the requested target widths and themes. Asset source/target hashes match all 23 manifest records. Hold final website-art acceptance until the legacy home/fallback header requirement is resolved or explicitly removed from scope; public publication remains separately gated.
